gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the NuPhy Air75 V3 and Node75 take only Gateron Low-profile 3.0 (and NuPhy Panda nano) switches because of what NuPhy calls "pin structure limitations", so switches from the Air75 V2 it also recommended (Low-profile 2.0 only) do not fit the V3, and Lofree's Kailh switches sit on a narrower terminal spacing again: "hot-swappable" on a low-profile board means three separate switch families, not one.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com (cited), mechkeyfoundry.com best-low-profile and keeb-finder.com's Air75 V2 / K3 Max / Air75 V3 compare (cited). mkbguide already says the Lofree boards are hot-swappable only "within Lofree's low-profile ecosystem" and ties the Air75 V3 to "Gateron/NuPhy Low-Profile 3.0 'Nano' switches"; mechkeyfoundry says the V3 "takes Gateron low-profile 3.0 switches" and that MX switches will not seat in any of them. None gives the reason (pin structure, terminal spacing), none says V2 switches do not fit the V3, and keeb-finder lists all three boards as simply "Hot-swappable Yes". The cited RTINGS roundup and Wirecutter page could not be read (RTINGS returned navigation only through the fetcher), so a cited rival may hold more than I could see.
decides: It does not change the overall pick; it settles one segment. A shopper who wants to change switches later gets the smallest menu on Lofree (Lofree x Kailh sets, $59 a box on lofree.co), a 3.0-only menu on the Air75 V3 and Node75, and the Gateron Low Profile 2.0 family on the K3 Max (Keychron sells that set from $11.19 today), and only on the K3 Max's RGB hot-swappable version. Lofree boards therefore win on the switch they ship with, not on swap options, and the page should say so in the Lofree row. It also corrects ChatGPT's second answer, which treats the Air75 V2 and V3 as sharing a "switch ecosystem".
